chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Asheym, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about Dhul-Fiqar, the sword of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he said: 'Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended with it from the sky, and its hilt was made of silver.'

key_terms.ذِي الْفَقَارِ: Dhul-Fiqar, the famous sword of the Prophet Muhammad
key_terms.سَيْفِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Sword of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the origin and material composition of the sword Dhul-Fiqar according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (as), the celestial origin of Dhul-Fiqar is confirmed, with the angel Gabriel (as) descending with the sword, highlighting its divine selection for the Prophet (saw). The specific mention of the silver hilt provides a tangible detail often cited in discussions regarding the physical attributes of the Prophet's arms. This tradition underscores the spiritual significance of Dhul-Fiqar as a symbol of divine authority and victory in Shia tradition.
